project.title: Climate Hack 2022
project.summary: Submission for Climate Hack 2022 — placed 14th out of over 130 participants.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: My submission for Climate Hack 2022. I built a deep learning model using PyTorch to predict solar power output from satellite imagery and weather data, helping optimize grid storage.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.body: A convolutional neural network ingests satellite cloud-cover images, while a separate MLP processes numerical weather forecasts. The two branches are fused and regressed to a solar power output value.

sections.title: Planning
sections.body: The hackathon timeline was 48 hours. We split work into data preprocessing, model architecture, training, and submission packaging, with daily checkpoint merges.

sections.title: Demo
sections.body: Code and trained weights are available on GitHub.
